newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends softer, c.bank seen capping rise.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends softer, c.bank seen capping rise.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,500-1,506 per dollar, down from the morning's 1,490-1,500 and from 1,498-1,508 at the previous close as the central bank was seen capping its rise, dealers said.

"The central bank started bidding for dollars slightly above 1,500 levs at midday, halting the lev rise and locking trade in a narrow range for the rest of the day," one dealer said. BNB officials were not available for comment.
The lev could have continued advancing towards 1,400 today if the central bank had capped the rise amid the persistently high foreign currency supply from clients, dealers said.

Traders said relatively large foreign currency volumes have started flowing in the country's banks from abroad recently as foreign investors opted for high-yield lev investments now that international lenders have pledged fresh funding to Bulgaria.

The main interest rate is now set at 14.15 percent monthly or 169.80 percent annually by the central bank, based on the effective average monthly yield of one-week discount T-bills sold by the Finance ministry last week.
The lev has traded stable between 1,500-1,600 for more than a month now and monthly inflation slowed to 12.3 percent in March from 242.7 percent in February.

Bulgaria has agreed a package of credits worth nearly $1.2 billion with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) , the World Bank, the European Union and the G-24 industrialised countries. -- Sofia Newsroom, (359-2) 91188
